Cc: tamara.lewis@cinderpoint.com, ops@cinderpoint.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:12:03 -0800
Subject: [URGENT] Production p95 spike impacting clinician workflow

Jonas,

We started seeing a sustained p95 latency increase (~1.6s -> 4.8s) on our on-prem Redwood cluster after the 03:00 maintenance window. This is crossing our contract SLA (p95 < 3s) and is causing UI timeouts for clinicians in the triage queue. We attached the support bundle.

What we know so far:
- Spike began ~03:10 PT and persisted across three nodes in the primary pool.
- Error rates are low (502s ~0.2%) but timeouts are up, which is impacting throughput.
- We reverted a minor model quantization change at 04:00 but latencies remain elevated.

We need immediate remediation steps and an ETA for either a hotpatch or an actionable rollback plan. If this will hit the SLA materially we need this escalated to your leadership ASAP — our CFO is watching the SLAs closely for next week's exec review.

Attachments: cinderpoint_support_bundle_20261107.tar.gz, p95_latency_snapshot_20261107.pdf

Thanks,
Alex Gonzalez
VP Engineering, CinderPoint Health

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:42:50 -08:00
Subject: Re: RE: [URGENT] Production p95 spike impacting clinician workflow

Jonas / Marissa,

Preliminary diagnostics from the support bundle:
- Observed an elevation in kernel scheduling latencies on nodes n-3/n-5 (htop traces attached).
- KV cache hit rates decreased slightly; more cold starts in tail window (03:08 - 03:22).
- One node shows an unexpected driver-level soft reset (dmesg lines included) coincident with the spike.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
A) Hotpatch kernel scheduler tweak (low risk, brief rolling reboots). Requires a signed hotpatch diff (I can prepare) and a 30-min maintenance window. Expected p95 improvement: ~40-60%.
B) Roll back to pre-quantization runtime build we shipped last week (higher throughput cost but fastest rollback path). Node drains + restart, ~45-60 min outage per node during restart window.
C) Traffic shaping to fallback model (smaller model) at the router — minimal infra changes, but could introduce quality regressions; immediate and reversible.

I recommend path A + short traffic shaping to reduce immediate load while we validate the hotpatch. I'll draft the patch and smoke tests.

Attachments: hotpatch_kernel.diff (draft), naomi_diag_htop_03_08.txt

Naomi
Director, Infrastructure Optimization
Redwood Inference
